slides.title: From Rosetta to Top7: physics-based de novo design
slides.body:
**Protein design** asks the inverse of folding: given a desired 3D structure or function, find a sequence (or sequences) that will fold to it. The field has gone from a few hand-crafted examples in the 1990s to a deep-learning-driven design pipeline today.

**Top7 (Kuhlman + Baker 2003 *Science*)** — first fully de novo protein with a fold not found in nature. 93 aa α/β protein designed by **RosettaDesign**: alternating loops of (a) backbone sampling with Rosetta fragment assembly, (b) sequence design optimizing a knowledge-based + physics-based energy function (van der Waals, electrostatics, solvation, H-bonds, side-chain packing via rotamer libraries + dead-end elimination / Monte Carlo). Crystal structure RMSD 1.2 Å from design. Proved physics + statistics can compute a foldable + stable sequence from scratch.

**Rosetta framework** (Baker lab, 1997+):
- **Rosetta energy function (REF15)**: weighted sum of Lennard-Jones, Lazaridis-Karplus solvation, hydrogen-bond geometric terms, Dunbrack rotameric self-energy, electrostatics, Ramachandran propensities, disulfide geometry.
- **Monte Carlo + simulated annealing** in side-chain + backbone space; **fragment assembly** with 9-mer + 3-mer libraries from the PDB.
- **PyRosetta** Python bindings (Chaudhury 2010) opened the framework to non-experts.
- **Rosetta@home + Foldit** crowd-sourced design — Foldit produced a Mason-Pfizer monkey virus retroviral protease crystal structure (Cooper 2011).

**Hyperstable miniproteins** (Rocklin + Baker 2017 *Science*): designed > 15 000 small (~40 aa) α-helical + β-sheet miniproteins; high-throughput **yeast surface display + protease degradation** screen as a stability proxy; thousands confirmed stable + monomeric — proving design success rates improve with massively parallel experiment-in-the-loop training data.

**Designed enzymes (Rosetta era)**:
- **Retro-aldolases** (Jiang + Baker 2008, Althoff 2012) — first computationally designed enzymes for non-natural Diels-Alder + retro-aldol reactions.
- **Diels-Alderases** (Siegel + Baker 2010), **Kemp eliminases** (Röthlisberger 2008; Khersonsky 2010-2012 directed-evolution boost).
- Initial k_cat/K_M 10²-10⁴ M⁻¹s⁻¹ (vs 10⁶-10⁹ for natural enzymes) — improvable by directed evolution after designing the scaffold.

**De novo binders to therapeutic targets** (Chevalier + Baker 2017; Cao + Baker 2020 *Science*): computationally designed miniproteins (~40-65 aa) targeting **IL-2R**, **PD-1**, **HER2**, **VEGF-R**, **SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD** (LCB1 picomolar; protective in mouse model). Workflow: pick target patch → generate diverse backbone scaffolds → graft binding hotspots → design sequences → filter computationally → high-throughput yeast-display screening → affinity maturation.

**Baker lab milestones (pre-DL)**: 2003 Top7 first novel fold; 2008-2010 designed enzymes; 2014 self-assembling nanocages (King + Baker); 2017 hyperstable miniproteins + first computational SARS-CoV-2 binders. Showed the design problem could be tackled computationally if you accept modest but non-zero success rates + iterate experimentally.

slides.title: RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN: the generative-AI revolution
slides.body:
**2022-2023 leap**: generative diffusion models for backbone generation + deep-learning inverse folding for sequence design — pushing experimental success rates from ~1% to 10-50%.

**ProteinMPNN** (Dauparas + Baker 2022 *Science* — 'Robust deep learning–based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN'):
- **Inverse folding**: given a 3D backbone, generate a sequence that will fold to it.
- Graph neural network over Cα + backbone atoms; message passing over k-nearest-neighbor edges with relative-position encoding; trained on PDB to predict residue identities from backbone geometry.
- **Experimental success rate ~40-60%** for native + de novo backbones — far above Rosetta-only baselines (~5-10%).
- Drop-in replacement for RosettaDesign in modern pipelines.
- Variants: **LigandMPNN** (Dauparas 2023) for protein-ligand co-design; **SolubleMPNN** for solubility bias; **AbMPNN** for antibody CDRs.

**ESM-IF** (Hsu + Rives 2022, Meta): inverse folding using ESM language-model representations; comparable to ProteinMPNN, MSA-free.

**RFdiffusion** (Watson + Juergens + Bennett + Trippe + Baker 2023 *Nature* — 'De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion'):
- **Denoising diffusion model** built on **RoseTTAFold** weights.
- Trained by reversing a Gaussian noise process applied to PDB backbone coordinates.
- **Generates novel backbones** conditioned on: length, symmetry (cyclic, dihedral), hotspot residues for binders, topological scaffolds (helical bundles, β-barrels), motif scaffolding (preserving an active-site motif while designing the rest).
- After backbone generation → ProteinMPNN designs sequence → AF2 validates fold confidence (designs accepted if AF2 pLDDT > 80 + RMSD < 2 Å from RFdiffusion target).
- **Experimental success 5-50%** on binders + scaffolds — orders of magnitude better than prior methods.
- **Wicky 2022, Bennett 2023**: hundreds of de novo SARS-CoV-2 spike + IL-2R + IL-23R binders validated.
- **Glasscock + Baker 2023**: de novo enzyme scaffolds with RFdiffusion + LigandMPNN.

**Chroma** (Ingraham + Baker + Generate Biomedicines 2023 *Nature*): diffusion over backbones + sequences jointly; text-prompt-style conditioning on symmetry + length + class.

**Frame-based diffusion**: **FrameDiff** (Yim 2023), **Genie** (Lin 2023) — diffusion over SE(3) residue frames (position + orientation), leveraging Invariant Point Attention from AF2.

**Flow matching + score-based alternatives**:
- **FoldFlow / Multiflow** (Bose 2023, Campbell 2024).
- **ProteinSGM**, **EigenFold** (Jing 2023).

**Validation tools**: **Boltz, Chai-1, AlphaFold 3** for structure + affinity prediction.

**Pipeline (modern Baker-lab style)**:
1. Define target: binder hotspot, enzyme active site, symmetric scaffold, motif of interest.
2. **RFdiffusion** generates many backbones (10⁴-10⁶) under constraints.
3. **ProteinMPNN** designs sequences (multiple per backbone).
4. **AF2 / ESMFold** filters by predicted self-consistency (pLDDT, RMSD to target).
5. **Rosetta + ML scoring** for energetics + ligand binding.
6. Top hundreds → **synthesized + tested** (gene synthesis, expression in E. coli or mammalian cells, yeast display or biochemical assays).
7. **Affinity maturation** by additional design rounds + saturating mutagenesis.

slides.title: Applications: binders, enzymes, vaccines, plastic-degrading proteins
slides.body:
**Therapeutic de novo binders**:
- **SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD**: Cao + Baker 2020 *Science* picomolar miniprotein binders (LCB1 ~6 nM, LCB3); LCB1 inhalable formulation as candidate therapeutic; AHB2 + minibinder designs neutralized variants. Linsky + Vorobieva 2020 designed ACE2-mimic binders. RFdiffusion era (Wicky 2022, Bennett 2023) extended to dozens of viral targets.
- **IL-2R / IL-23R**: Silva + Baker 2019 *Nature* designed IL-2 mimics bypassing the toxic IL-2Rα subunit — Neoleukin NL-201 entered clinical trials for cancer immunotherapy.
- **PD-1 + checkpoint mimics**: designed minibinders as oral/topical alternatives to mAbs.
- **TrkB agonists, IgE blockers, complement inhibitors** in pipeline.

**Designed enzymes**:
- **Retro-aldolases + Diels-Alderases** (Jiang 2008; Siegel 2010): first computational enzymes for non-natural reactions.
- **Kemp eliminases**: > 10⁶-fold improvement by combining design + directed evolution.
- **Luciferases — LuxSit + LuxSit-i** (Yeh + Baker 2023 *Nature*): de novo small designed luciferases (~13 kDa) that emit light upon substrate binding; smaller + more tunable than Renilla or firefly. Enables custom bioluminescent reporters.
- **PETase / hydrolase improvements**: original IsPETase (Yoshida 2016) found in soil bacteria; **FAST-PETase** (Lu + Alper 2022 *Nature*) ML-guided thermostable variant degrades PET bottles to monomers in days; Carbios pilot plant deployment 2024.

**Designed vaccines + antigen scaffolds**:
- **RSV F prefusion stabilization**: McLellan + Graham + Kwong 2013 *Science* used structure-based cavity-filling to stabilize the metastable prefusion conformation of RSV F — basis for FDA-approved RSV vaccines (Abrysvo, Arexvy 2023). Same principle applied to SARS-CoV-2 spike (S-2P → HexaPro) in the Pfizer-BioNTech + Moderna mRNA vaccines.
- **HIV Env stabilization**: SOSIP trimers (Sanders + Moore 2013) + designed bnAb-epitope scaffolds.
- **Self-assembling protein nanoparticles** (King + Baker 2014, 2016): 60-mer + 120-mer icosahedral nanocages display antigens at high valency. Used in IcosaVax + SK Bioscience SKYCovione COVID vaccine + influenza HA + RSV F display vaccines.
- **AlphaFold + RFdiffusion** generating scaffolds for next-generation universal influenza + pan-coronavirus + HIV vaccines.

**Industrial enzymes + sustainability**:
- **PETase + MHETase** for plastic recycling.
- **CO₂-fixing carbonic anhydrase variants** for carbon capture.
- **Detergent proteases, lipases** with improved thermostability.
- **Cellulases + xylanases** for biofuel.
- **Designed metalloenzymes** mimicking nitrogenase, hydrogenase for green chemistry.

**Self-assembling nanostructures** (King + Baker 2014-2024): icosahedral cages, helical filaments, tetrahedra by symmetric docking + ProteinMPNN; optical sensors, drug-delivery cages.

**Designed protein switches + logic** (Langan + Boyken + Baker 2019 *Nature* — LOCKR): designed allosteric switches where a 'key' peptide displaces an autoinhibitory 'latch' — enabling protein-level logic gates, signaling networks, sensors.

**Computational antibody design**:
- **RFantibody** (Bennett + Baker 2024): RFdiffusion variant for de novo antibody CDR loops + nanobody scaffolds.
- **AbMPNN, AbLang, AntiBERTy**: sequence-level antibody language models.
- **AlphaFold-Multimer / AF3** for antibody-antigen interface prediction.
- Combined with phage + yeast display libraries for affinity maturation.

**The 2024 Chemistry Nobel** went to **David Baker** for de novo protein design, jointly with Hassabis + Jumper for AlphaFold — recognizing the unification of structure prediction + design as a single deep-learning-driven discipline.

question.question: Design a SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD binder
question.goal: Design a 60-aa de novo miniprotein binder for the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD ACE2-binding interface. Walk through scaffold generation, sequence design, in-silico filtering, and experimental validation.

steps.motivation: Hotspot selection defines the design problem.

acceptedAnswers: ACE2-binding residues (K417, F456, F486, N487, Y489, Q493, Y505) as hotspots; small α-helical bundle scaffolds (3 helix, like LCB1)

hints: What residues on RBD contact ACE2?
What scaffold class did Cao + Baker 2020 LCB1 use?
steps.reveal: Hotspots: K417, F456, F486, N487, Y489, Q493, Y505 — the ACE2 receptor-binding ridge + tip. Scaffold: small α-helical bundle (3-helix, ~60 aa) — Cao + Baker 2020 LCB1 used this class. Condition RFdiffusion on those hotspot positions + helix bundle topology.

acceptedAnswers: RFdiffusion 10^4-10^5 backbones conditioned on hotspots; ProteinMPNN ~8 sequences per backbone; predict folding with AF2 single-sequence

hints: How many backbones do you need + how do you design sequences?
steps.reveal: Run RFdiffusion ~10⁴-10⁵ times conditioned on hotspots + helix bundle topology — produces diverse novel backbones presenting the hotspots on a binding face. For each backbone, run ProteinMPNN ~8 times to generate diverse sequences (temperature 0.1-0.3). Predict each sequence's fold with AF2 in single-sequence mode (no MSA) — high pLDDT + low RMSD to RFdiffusion target = designs likely to fold as intended.

acceptedAnswers: AF2 pLDDT > 80, RMSD < 2 Å to design, AF-Multimer ipTM > 0.7 for binder-RBD complex, Rosetta ΔG_binding favorable, surface solubility + low aggregation

hints: Self-consistency (AF2 vs design), complex confidence (AF-Multimer), energetics.
steps.reveal: Filter cascade: (1) AF2 single-sequence pLDDT > 80 + Cα RMSD < 2 Å to RFdiffusion target (self-consistency); (2) AF-Multimer or AF3 ipTM > 0.7 + interface-PAE < 5 Å for binder-RBD complex; (3) Rosetta ΔG_binding < -30 REU; (4) surface hydrophilicity + no exposed hydrophobic patches; (5) sequence diversity for ~96-well synthesis.

acceptedAnswers: synthesize ~10^2 genes; yeast surface display screening with fluorescent RBD; deep-sequence enriched binders; characterize top hits by BLI/SPR + size-exclusion + cryo-EM or co-crystal

hints: How do you screen ~10^2 candidates fast?
steps.reveal: Synthesize ~10² candidate genes; express in E. coli or yeast surface display (Aga1p/Aga2p anchor); incubate cells with fluorescent RBD; FACS-enrich high-binding cells over multiple rounds; deep-sequence to track enriched binders. Characterize top hits by BLI (Octet) or SPR (Biacore) for K_D (~nM expected); SEC-MALS for monomer/aggregate; cryo-EM or co-crystal for atomic confirmation. Affinity-mature winners by saturating mutagenesis + further design rounds.

question.question: Why did RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN transform de novo protein design?
options: Pre-2022 design (Rosetta-only) had ~1-5% experimental success rates: designs often misfolded, aggregated, or bound the wrong epitope. **RFdiffusion** (Watson + Baker 2023 *Nature*) reformulates backbone generation as a **denoising diffusion process** on PDB-derived backbone coordinates — built on RoseTTAFold weights. It generates diverse, novel backbones from scratch under flexible conditioning (length, symmetry, hotspot residues, motif scaffolding, topological class). **ProteinMPNN** (Dauparas + Baker 2022 *Science*) replaces RosettaDesign for sequence design: a graph neural network on Cα + backbone atoms predicts residue identities consistent with the backbone, achieving ~40-60% experimental success (vs ~5-10% for Rosetta). The combination — RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AF2 self-consistency filtering — pushes overall design success to 10-50% for binders, enzyme scaffolds, symmetric assemblies, antibody CDRs (RFantibody). Empirically validated on hundreds of SARS-CoV-2 spike binders (Wicky 2022, Bennett 2023), IL-2/IL-23R binders, de novo luciferases (LuxSit, Yeh 2023), plastic-degrading enzymes (FAST-PETase). David Baker's 2024 Chemistry Nobel recognized this unified deep-learning-driven design discipline.
question.explanation: RFdiffusion (Watson + Baker 2023 *Nature*) — denoising diffusion on PDB backbones, conditioned on hotspots/symmetry/motifs. ProteinMPNN (Dauparas + Baker 2022 *Science*) — GNN inverse folding ~40-60% success vs ~5-10% Rosetta. Combined with AF2 self-consistency filtering, push experimental success to 10-50% for binders, enzymes, symmetric assemblies, antibody CDRs. Baker 2024 Nobel.

question.question: Design a new enzyme scaffold
question.prompt: You need a thermostable de novo retro-aldolase that catalyzes cleavage of a specific β-hydroxy ketone substrate with k_cat/K_M > 10³ M⁻¹s⁻¹. Walk through the design strategy: (a) catalytic motif (e.g., Lys-based Schiff-base mechanism vs metal-coordinated); (b) scaffold generation by RFdiffusion motif-scaffolding around the catalytic residues; (c) sequence design by LigandMPNN with substrate analog; (d) AF3 or Boltz for in-silico catalysis validation; (e) experimental pipeline including directed evolution rounds. Comment on realistic catalytic activity expectations + when to involve directed evolution.

question.question: If RFdiffusion generates 10⁵ backbones, each with 8 ProteinMPNN sequences, AF2 self-consistency passes 5%, AF-Multimer ipTM filter passes 20%, and Rosetta passes 30%, how many designs do you order for synthesis?

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how de novo protein design evolved from Rosetta Top7 (2003) to the RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN pipeline (2023) + name three Nobel-noted applications.
question.rubric: Mentions: Kuhlman + Baker Top7 (2003 *Science*) first novel fold designed with RosettaDesign physics-based scoring. Rosetta era: hyperstable miniproteins (Rocklin 2017), designed enzymes (retro-aldolases Jiang 2008, Diels-Alderases Siegel 2010, Kemp eliminases Röthlisberger 2008), nanocages (King + Baker 2014), de novo binders (LCB1 SARS-CoV-2 Cao 2020, IL-2 mimics Silva 2019). 2022-2023 deep-learning revolution: ProteinMPNN (Dauparas + Baker 2022 *Science*) GNN inverse folding ~40-60% experimental success; RFdiffusion (Watson + Baker 2023 *Nature*) denoising diffusion on PDB backbones conditioned on hotspots/symmetry/motifs. Pipeline: RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → AF2 self-consistency → synthesis + yeast-display screening → affinity maturation. Applications: SARS-CoV-2 + IL-2R + IL-23R binders, LuxSit designed luciferases (Yeh 2023), FAST-PETase plastic degradation (Lu + Alper 2022), RSV F prefusion-stabilized vaccines (McLellan 2013 → Abrysvo/Arexvy 2023), HexaPro spike for mRNA COVID vaccines, IcosaVax nanoparticle vaccines. David Baker 2024 Chemistry Nobel jointly with Hassabis + Jumper for protein design + AlphaFold. Concludes: structure prediction + design are now one discipline driven by deep learning + experimental validation.
